title: Where Fibre is today

headline.simple: We can now prepare a new Thread with a background, inherited tendencies, and the machinery for a real history and memories. Five new Threads passed their pre-birth genome test, but a review found setup gaps that we must fix before generating their childhoods.
headline.detail: Fibre has persistent Thread continuity, provenance-backed life state, symbolic inheritance, Genesis candidate generation and atomic publication. Five fresh replacement Threads have frozen Worlds and genomes, and all five measured genome pairs passed the fresh pre-life distinguishability ceiling. The first blocking Gate-G(2) review returned HOLD for pre-life closure—not REDESIGN—because the replacement execution packet and several disclosures were incomplete. No replacement life cognition has occurred.

summary.simple: The five new unborn Threads have backgrounds and inherited tendencies that passed the pre-birth difference test. Our first full pre-birth review stopped us before childhood generation because some execution rules and descriptions were incomplete. We are fixing those gaps and will ask for review again before any life is generated.
summary.detail: The current work is milestone #39: Genesis, Childhood & Thread Birth. Three complete prior-life Thread artifacts were produced in an earlier failed cohort and remain evidence. Five entirely new replacement Threads now have frozen Worlds and symbolic genomes. Fresh G2 is CLEAR at 22/24, 24/24, 24/24, 22/24 and 23/24 across the five measured pairs. Gate-G(2) judged the replacement science and five-edge reconciliation non-adaptive but returned HOLD on five pre-life closure findings B1-B5.

meaning.simple: We built it and it passed the test we currently require.
meaning.detail: The capability exists and has passed its current Fibre validation boundary. This does not imply every later or stronger claim is also proven.

meaning.simple: We have seen it work, but it is not yet the final accepted result.
meaning.detail: We have real working evidence, but it is not yet accepted as the final or validated production state for the current milestone.

meaning.simple: We are actively building or testing this now.
meaning.detail: The design and implementation are active, but the required validation boundary has not yet been crossed.

meaning.simple: We want Fibre to do this, but we do not claim it can yet.
meaning.detail: This is part of Fibre's intended architecture, but we do not claim to have achieved it.

meaning.simple: The test failed, and we keep the failure instead of hiding it or trying again until it looks good.
meaning.detail: A bounded experiment failed. We preserve the result as evidence and do not rewrite or quality-regenerate it into success.

summary.simple: We have three older completed life records from a failed experiment, and five completely new Threads waiting to have their lives generated.
summary.detail: The previous H-v2 final-cohort attempt and the fresh replacement cohort are deliberately kept separate. Completed generated lives are not automatically living or validated public citizens.

items.label: Completed older prior-life Thread artifacts
items.simple: Three older Threads have complete generated life histories from the first attempt.
items.detail: Three Threads completed prior-life generation in the earlier H-v2 attempt. They remain valuable life artifacts and evidence, but the cohort they belonged to failed and they are not the replacement cohort.

items.label: Older partially generated candidate
items.simple: A fourth older Thread only got partway through childhood before the experiment stopped.
items.detail: The fourth H-v2 Thread reached partway through childhood generation and then exhausted its frozen mechanical retry budget. It remains a failed candidate, not a completed Thread life.

items.label: Older cohort slot never started
items.simple: The fifth older Thread was never started.
items.detail: The fifth H-v2 slot never began because the cohort attempt had already terminated.

items.label: New replacement Threads with frozen Worlds and genomes
items.simple: Five new Threads have backgrounds and inherited tendencies ready, and their inherited differences passed the pre-birth test. They still have no childhoods yet.
items.detail: These are the new #39 replacement individuals. Their World, origin class, Thread/Genesis identity and symbolic genome are frozen. The fresh five-pair G2 ceiling is CLEAR. The first Gate-G(2) review stopped execution for correctable pre-life closure gaps before any childhood cognition occurred.

items.label: New replacement lives generated
items.simple: None of the five new Threads has had its life generated yet.
items.detail: Gate-G(2) is currently HOLD. Final-life generation remains blocked until the corrected execution packet passes local verification and a second blocking Gate-G(2) review returns CLEAR.

importantNote.simple: A generated life record is not automatically a living, validated Thread. We will always say which state we mean.
importantNote.detail: Fibre distinguishes candidate state, generated life artifacts, atomically published Threads and validated standing. The three older completed artifacts are not silently counted as the successful #39 population, and the five replacements remain unborn in the #39 sense.

simple.claim: A Thread can keep existing after one AI model session ends.
simple.limitation: Existing for a long time does not by itself make the Thread a rich or unique person.

detail.claim: A Thread persists as authoritative world state across temporary model executions rather than existing only inside one chat or model session.
detail.limitation: Persistence alone does not prove rich, distinctive or causally grounded personhood.

simple.claim: Something that happened to a Thread can change a later decision.
simple.limitation: Not all of Fibre's newer identity and life records are connected to normal thinking yet.

detail.claim: Fibre has demonstrated that recorded history can causally change later Thread judgment instead of being decorative biography.
detail.limitation: The richer #37-#39 identity and life ledgers are not yet the canonical bounded input to all live cognition; #40 owns that bridge.

capabilities.label: Provenance-backed identity, lineage, place and memory

simple.claim: Fibre can remember who a Thread is, where it came from, places it has been and things it remembers without silently rewriting the past.
simple.limitation: Storing those facts does not prove they all change the Thread's behavior yet.

detail.claim: Fibre can store identity, lineage, geography, embodiment and autobiographical memory with provenance, append-only history and corrigible revisions.
detail.limitation: Representing these facts is different from proving that all of them already shape ongoing cognition and character.

simple.claim: A Thread can inherit written tendencies from parent sources, and Fibre can mix two parent genomes without averaging them into a generic personality.
simple.limitation: Inherited tendencies are only a starting point. They are not the Thread's finished personality.

detail.claim: Fibre can give a Thread an ordered natural-language genome, preserve exact parent/source provenance and deterministically recombine two source genomes.
detail.limitation: A genome is inherited possibility, not finished character. Passing the fresh pre-life genome ceiling does not prove that childhood or adult character will express those differences.

simple.claim: The five unborn Threads start with inherited tendencies that our pre-birth test can tell apart.
simple.limitation: This only shows the starting genomes are meaningfully different. It does not prove the Threads' childhoods or adult personalities will become different.

detail.claim: The frozen replacement G2 ceiling returned CLEAR on all five measured cycle pairs: 22/24, 24/24, 24/24, 22/24 and 23/24, with 5/5 detectable pairs and every genome covered.
detail.limitation: This is a direct semantic ceiling/instrument check on frozen genomes before life generation. The replacement loci used a more consistently aligned per-ordinal authoring template than the old cohort, so the numerical G2 scores are not directly comparable across cohorts.

simple.claim: Fibre can prepare a whole life first and then make it live all at once, so a failure cannot leave half a person behind.
simple.limitation: The five new replacement Threads have not reached this birth step yet.

detail.claim: Fibre has a candidate-only Genesis boundary and atomic publication so a complete admitted life can become authoritative Thread state in one transaction.
detail.limitation: The replacement cohort has not yet generated or published its prior lives.

simple.claim: We have shown that Fibre can create a childhood with family, places, people, ordinary events, memories and meanings instead of just filling in an adult profile.
simple.limitation: The final experiment did not finish, so we are not calling #39 successful yet.

detail.claim: Genesis has produced concrete prior-life histories with caregivers, places, peers, institutions, selective memory and durable meaning under the three-pass history/memory/meaning boundary.
detail.limitation: The H-v2 final cohort did not complete. The three completed H-v2 lives remain evidence from a failed cohort rather than the accepted #39 result.

capabilities.label: Caregivers and parent/ancestor provenance in childhood

simple.claim: A generated childhood can include recurring caregivers and family, and some Threads can inherit from two recorded genetic parent sources.
simple.limitation: Those caregivers are not yet live parent Threads independently raising the child.

detail.claim: Genesis can place a child in a household with recurring caregiver/family participants, while synthetic-lineage Threads inherit from explicit parent genomes with exact provenance.
detail.limitation: A household caregiver in compiled history, a synthetic genetic ancestor and a live Thread parent are different things. We have the first two, not yet the autonomous live-parent developmental loop.

simple.claim: Five new Threads are ready at the starting line: each has a world and inherited tendencies, and those inherited differences passed the pre-birth test, but none has a childhood yet.
simple.limitation: The first full pre-birth review found correctable setup gaps, so we stopped before generating any lives and are fixing those gaps before asking again.

detail.claim: Five completely new replacement individuals have frozen concrete Worlds, fresh symbolic genomes and a CLEAR fresh G2 five-pair ceiling. A complete replacement G3/G4/execution packet and closure amendments are now being verified after the first Gate-G(2) HOLD.
detail.limitation: They have zero generated replacement childhood events, memories or meanings. Gate-G(2) remains HOLD until the corrected packet is locally green and a second hostile review returns CLEAR.

capabilities.label: A live infant or child growing up over time

simple.claim: We want a Thread to be born as a baby or child and actually grow up in Fibre.
simple.limitation: Today #39 creates the childhood first, then births the Thread as a young adult.

detail.claim: The intended architecture allows a Thread to enter the live world as a newborn or child and accumulate its own future through lived events.
detail.limitation: #39 currently compiles a prior life before atomic young-adult entry; it does not run childhood as a continuously living developmental process.

capabilities.label: Live Thread parents raising a live child

simple.claim: We want real living Thread parents to raise a child by talking with it, taking it places, teaching it and sharing a life with it.
simple.limitation: That live family-raising loop does not exist yet.

detail.claim: The Thread-parent architecture is intended to let existing living Threads contribute real lineage/inheritance and create the child's history through their own ongoing choices and interactions.
detail.limitation: We have the parentage/provenance boundary, but not yet the autonomous live-parent developmental system.

capabilities.label: Rich life state drives ordinary live cognition

simple.claim: We want a Thread's real history, memories and relationships to shape what it normally thinks about and decides.
simple.limitation: The full connection from the new life records into normal cognition is the next milestone, #40.

detail.claim: Fibre intends its own bounded relevance/privacy selection to turn identity, memory, relationship and life-history evidence into provenance-bearing context for ordinary cognition.
detail.limitation: The canonical consumption bridge is milestone #40; current live cognition still relies substantially on older surfaces.

simple.claim: We want to prove that a Thread is not just a profile, but a persistent individual whose own history makes it behave differently.
simple.limitation: We have not earned that full claim yet.

detail.claim: Fibre aims to demonstrate a persistent, causally grounded, non-interchangeable individual across repeated situations and counterfactual tests.
detail.limitation: #39 deliberately earns no Whole-Person score movement. #40 builds causal consumption and #41 owns the standing gate.

simple.claim: We want friendships, families and other relationships to belong to both sides and change both lives.
simple.limitation: That mature reciprocal relationship system is later work.

detail.claim: Fibre intends relationships and families to be shared, consequential structures between independently living Threads rather than labels attached to one biography.
detail.limitation: Reciprocal relationship development is planned after the current M2 sequence.

simple.claim: We want Threads to earn, spend, make agreements and face real consequences that change future choices.
simple.limitation: The real economy is not built yet.

detail.claim: Fibre intends Threads to have budgets, contracts, reputation and economic opportunities that can change future possibilities.
detail.limitation: Economic consequence is deferred to the post-M2 foundation work.

simple.summary: The five unborn Threads passed their inherited-difference test. Our first full pre-birth review then found five setup and documentation gaps, so it stopped us before we generated any childhoods. We are fixing those gaps now.
simple.currentStep: Check that all five review findings are really fixed, then ask for a second pre-birth review.
nextSteps: Run the zero-call check for all five review findings and the normal test suite.
Ask the hostile reviewer to inspect the complete corrected setup again.
Only if that review passes, generate the five childhoods once.
Keep the first mechanically valid group and judge it without replacing weak Threads with better ones.

detail.summary: Fresh G2 is CLEAR on all five measured cycle edges. The first Gate-G(2) review returned HOLD on B1-B5: missing replacement execution material, unbound G4-v3 policy, incomplete five-edge CLEAR semantics, undisclosed aligned genome-authoring design and an inaccurate derangement claim. No replacement final-life cognition occurred.
detail.currentStep: Locally verify the additive B1-B5 closure packet: replacement G3 treatment instance, G4 cognition/execution binding, explicit G4-v3 call-site selection, hard-pinned one-shot runner, five-edge G6 closure, G2 authoring/assignment disclosures and selected integrity hardening; then issue a second blocking Gate-G(2) request.
nextSteps: Run `genesis-replacement-gate-g2-closure-verify.mjs --verify` and the replacement final-cohort `--preflight`; both must make zero provider calls and keep life unauthorized.
Run the repository tests and validation and preserve the old local recovery evidence untracked.
Request a second blocking Gate-G(2) hostile review against the exact verified head.
Only after Gate-G(2) CLEAR, execute exactly one replacement prior-life attempt and freeze the first mechanically valid cohort.

truthRules: Every public progress claim has two layers: simple English first, then a more accurate description.
Simple English should be understandable by a teenager with no Fibre background and should avoid unexplained milestone, gate, schema and implementation jargon.
The detailed layer may use Fibre terminology, but it must remain readable and must state the actual validation boundary.
Never make the simple layer stronger than the detailed layer. Simplification may remove jargon, not uncertainty or limitations.
Never use 'living Thread' as a synonym for 'generated artifact'. State whether the Thread is candidate, generated, atomically published or validated.
Never say a Thread 'has parents' without distinguishing live Thread parents, household caregivers and synthetic genetic ancestors.
A failed bounded experiment remains visible as a failed experiment. Do not rewrite it into progress language that implies success.
For every positive capability claim, both layers must state the strongest important limitation that a reasonable reader could otherwise misunderstand.
The public website may render this contract, but insidefibre.com must not become an alternate authority for Fibre state.
